# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/infer/0.19.0/src/infer/lib.rs.html

# infer/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)/*!
[2](https://docs.rs#2)Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[3](https://docs.rs#3)[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.
[4](https://docs.rs#4)
[5](https://docs.rs#5)# Examples
[6](https://docs.rs#6)
[7](https://docs.rs#7)### Get the type of a buffer
[8](https://docs.rs#8)
[9](https://docs.rs#9)```rust
[10](https://docs.rs#10)let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
[11](https://docs.rs#11)let kind = infer::get(&buf).expect("file type is known");
[12](https://docs.rs#12)
[13](https://docs.rs#13)assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "image/jpeg");
[14](https://docs.rs#14)assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "jpg");
[15](https://docs.rs#15)assert_eq!(kind.matcher_type(), infer::MatcherType::Image);
[16](https://docs.rs#16)```
[17](https://docs.rs#17)
[18](https://docs.rs#18)### Check file type by path
[19](https://docs.rs#19)
[20](https://docs.rs#20)```rust
[21](https://docs.rs#21)# #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[22](https://docs.rs#22)# fn run() {
[23](https://docs.rs#23)let kind = infer::get_from_path("testdata/sample.jpg")
[24](https://docs.rs#24)    .expect("file read successfully")
[25](https://docs.rs#25)    .expect("file type is known");
[26](https://docs.rs#26)
[27](https://docs.rs#27)assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "image/jpeg");
[28](https://docs.rs#28)assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "jpg");
[29](https://docs.rs#29)# }
[30](https://docs.rs#30)```
[31](https://docs.rs#31)
[32](https://docs.rs#32)### Check for specific type
[33](https://docs.rs#33)
[34](https://docs.rs#34)```rust
[35](https://docs.rs#35)let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
[36](https://docs.rs#36)assert!(infer::image::is_jpeg(&buf));
[37](https://docs.rs#37)```
[38](https://docs.rs#38)
[39](https://docs.rs#39)### Check for specific type class
[40](https://docs.rs#40)
[41](https://docs.rs#41)```rust
[42](https://docs.rs#42)let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
[43](https://docs.rs#43)assert!(infer::is_image(&buf));
[44](https://docs.rs#44)```
[45](https://docs.rs#45)
[46](https://docs.rs#46)### Adds a custom file type matcher
[47](https://docs.rs#47)
[48](https://docs.rs#48)Here we actually need to use the `Infer` struct to be able to declare custom matchers.
[49](https://docs.rs#49)
[50](https://docs.rs#50)```rust
[51](https://docs.rs#51)# #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[52](https://docs.rs#52)# fn run() {
[53](https://docs.rs#53)fn custom_matcher(buf: &[u8]) -> bool {
[54](https://docs.rs#54)    return buf.len() >= 3 && buf[0] == 0x10 && buf[1] == 0x11 && buf[2] == 0x12;
[55](https://docs.rs#55)}
[56](https://docs.rs#56)
[57](https://docs.rs#57)let mut info = infer::Infer::new();
[58](https://docs.rs#58)info.add("custom/foo", "foo", custom_matcher);
[59](https://docs.rs#59)
[60](https://docs.rs#60)let buf = [0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13];
[61](https://docs.rs#61)let kind = info.get(&buf).unwrap();
[62](https://docs.rs#62)
[63](https://docs.rs#63)assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "custom/foo");
[64](https://docs.rs#64)assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "foo");
[65](https://docs.rs#65)# }
[66](https://docs.rs#66)```
[67](https://docs.rs#67)*/

[93](https://docs.rs#93)/// All the supported matchers categorized and exposed as functions
[94](https://docs.rs#94)pub use matchers::*;
[95](https://docs.rs#95)
[96](https://docs.rs#96)/// Matcher function
[97](https://docs.rs#97)pub type Matcher = fn(buf: &[u8]) -> bool;
[98](https://docs.rs#98)
[99](https://docs.rs#99)/// Generic information for a type
[100](https://docs.rs#100)#[derive(Copy, Clone)]
[101](https://docs.rs#101)pub struct Type {
[102](https://docs.rs#102)    matcher_type: MatcherType,
[103](https://docs.rs#103)    mime_type: &'static str,
[104](https://docs.rs#104)    extension: &'static str,
[105](https://docs.rs#105)    matcher: WrapMatcher,
[106](https://docs.rs#106)}
[107](https://docs.rs#107)
[108](https://docs.rs#108)impl Type {
[109](https://docs.rs#109)    pub(crate) const fn new_static(
[110](https://docs.rs#110)        matcher_type: MatcherType,
[111](https://docs.rs#111)        mime_type: &'static str,
[112](https://docs.rs#112)        extension: &'static str,
[113](https://docs.rs#113)        matcher: WrapMatcher,
[114](https://docs.rs#114)    ) -> Self {
[115](https://docs.rs#115)        Self {
[116](https://docs.rs#116)            matcher_type,
[117](https://docs.rs#117)            mime_type,
[118](https://docs.rs#118)            extension,
[119](https://docs.rs#119)            matcher,
[120](https://docs.rs#120)        }
[121](https://docs.rs#121)    }
[122](https://docs.rs#122)
[123](https://docs.rs#123)    /// Returns a new `Type` with matcher and extension.
[124](https://docs.rs#124)    pub fn new(
[125](https://docs.rs#125)        matcher_type: MatcherType,
[126](https://docs.rs#126)        mime_type: &'static str,
[127](https://docs.rs#127)        extension: &'static str,
[128](https://docs.rs#128)        matcher: Matcher,
[129](https://docs.rs#129)    ) -> Self {
[130](https://docs.rs#130)        Self::new_static(matcher_type, mime_type, extension, WrapMatcher(matcher))
[131](https://docs.rs#131)    }
[132](https://docs.rs#132)
[133](https://docs.rs#133)    /// Returns the type of matcher
[134](https://docs.rs#134)    ///
[135](https://docs.rs#135)    /// # Examples
[136](https://docs.rs#136)    ///
[137](https://docs.rs#137)    /// ```rust
[138](https://docs.rs#138)    /// let info = infer::Infer::new();
[139](https://docs.rs#139)    /// let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
[140](https://docs.rs#140)    /// let kind = info.get(&buf).expect("file type is known");
[141](https://docs.rs#141)    ///
[142](https://docs.rs#142)    /// assert_eq!(kind.matcher_type(), infer::MatcherType::Image);
[143](https://docs.rs#143)    /// ```
[144](https://docs.rs#144)    pub const fn matcher_type(&self) -> MatcherType {
[145](https://docs.rs#145)        self.matcher_type
[146](https://docs.rs#146)    }
[147](https://docs.rs#147)
[148](https://docs.rs#148)    /// Returns the mime type
[149](https://docs.rs#149)    pub const fn mime_type(&self) -> &'static str {
[150](https://docs.rs#150)        self.mime_type
[151](https://docs.rs#151)    }
[152](https://docs.rs#152)
[153](https://docs.rs#153)    /// Returns the file extension
[154](https://docs.rs#154)    pub const fn extension(&self) -> &'static str {
[155](https://docs.rs#155)        self.extension
[156](https://docs.rs#156)    }
[157](https://docs.rs#157)
[158](https://docs.rs#158)    /// Checks if buf matches this Type
[159](https://docs.rs#159)    fn matches(&self, buf: &[u8]) -> bool {
[160](https://docs.rs#160)        (self.matcher.0)(buf)
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    }
[162](https://docs.rs#162)}
[163](https://docs.rs#163)
[164](https://docs.rs#164)impl fmt::Debug for Type {
[165](https://docs.rs#165)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[166](https://docs.rs#166)        f.debug_struct("Type")
[167](https://docs.rs#167)            .field("matcher_type", &self.matcher_type)
[168](https://docs.rs#168)            .field("mime_type", &self.mime_type)
[169](https://docs.rs#169)            .field("extension", &self.extension)
[170](https://docs.rs#170)            .finish()
[171](https://docs.rs#171)    }
[172](https://docs.rs#172)}
[173](https://docs.rs#173)
[174](https://docs.rs#174)impl fmt::Display for Type {

[177](https://docs.rs#177)    }
[178](https://docs.rs#178)}
[179](https://docs.rs#179)
[180](https://docs.rs#180)impl PartialEq for Type {
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
[182](https://docs.rs#182)        self.matcher_type == other.matcher_type
[183](https://docs.rs#183)            && self.mime_type == other.mime_type
[184](https://docs.rs#184)            && self.extension == other.extension
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    }
[186](https://docs.rs#186)}
[187](https://docs.rs#187)
[188](https://docs.rs#188)/// Infer allows to use a custom set of `Matcher`s for infering a MIME type.
[189](https://docs.rs#189)///
[190](https://docs.rs#190)/// Most operations can be done by using the _top level functions_, but when custom matchers
[191](https://docs.rs#191)/// are needed every call has to go through the `Infer` struct to be able
[192](https://docs.rs#192)/// to see the custom matchers.
[193](https://docs.rs#193)pub struct Infer {
[194](https://docs.rs#194)    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    mmap: Vec<Type>,
[196](https://docs.rs#196)}
[197](https://docs.rs#197)
[198](https://docs.rs#198)impl Infer {
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    /// Initialize a new instance of the infer struct.
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    pub const fn new() -> Infer {
[201](https://docs.rs#201)        #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[202](https://docs.rs#202)        return Infer { mmap: Vec::new() };
[203](https://docs.rs#203)
[204](https://docs.rs#204)        #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
[205](https://docs.rs#205)        return Infer {};
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    }
[207](https://docs.rs#207)
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    fn iter_matchers(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Type> {
[209](https://docs.rs#209)        let mmap = MATCHER_MAP.iter();
[210](https://docs.rs#210)
[211](https://docs.rs#211)        #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[212](https://docs.rs#212)        return self.mmap.iter().chain(mmap);
[213](https://docs.rs#213)
[214](https://docs.rs#214)        #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
[215](https://docs.rs#215)        return mmap;
[216](https://docs.rs#216)    }
[217](https://docs.rs#217)
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    /// Returns the file type of the buffer.
[219](https://docs.rs#219)    ///
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    /// # Examples
[221](https://docs.rs#221)    ///
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    /// ```rust
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    /// let info = infer::Infer::new();
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    /// let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    /// let kind = info.get(&buf).expect("file type is known");
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    ///
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    /// assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "image/jpeg");
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    /// assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "jpg");
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    /// ```
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    pub fn get(&self, buf: &[u8]) -> Option<Type> {
[231](https://docs.rs#231)        self.iter_matchers().find(|kind| kind.matches(buf)).copied()
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    }
[233](https://docs.rs#233)
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    /// Returns the file type of the file given a path.
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    ///
[236](https://docs.rs#236)    /// # Examples
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    ///
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    /// See [`get_from_path`](./fn.get_from_path.html).
[239](https://docs.rs#239)    #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    pub fn get_from_path<P: AsRef<Path>>(&self, path: P) -> io::Result<Option<Type>> {
[241](https://docs.rs#241)        let file = File::open(path)?;
[242](https://docs.rs#242)
[243](https://docs.rs#243)        let limit = file
[244](https://docs.rs#244)            .metadata()
[245](https://docs.rs#245)            .map(|m| std::cmp::min(m.len(), 8192) as usize + 1)
[246](https://docs.rs#246)            .unwrap_or(0);
[247](https://docs.rs#247)        let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(limit);
[248](https://docs.rs#248)        file.take(8192).read_to_end(&mut bytes)?;
[249](https://docs.rs#249)
[250](https://docs.rs#250)        Ok(self.get(&bytes))
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    }
[252](https://docs.rs#252)
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    /// Determines whether a buffer is of given extension.
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    ///
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    /// # Examples
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    ///
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    /// See [`is`](./fn.is.html).
[258](https://docs.rs#258)    pub fn is(&self, buf: &[u8], extension: &str) -> bool {
[259](https://docs.rs#259)        self.iter_matchers()
[260](https://docs.rs#260)            .any(|kind| kind.extension() == extension && kind.matches(buf))
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    }
[262](https://docs.rs#262)
[263](https://docs.rs#263)    /// Determines whether a buffer is of given mime type.
[264](https://docs.rs#264)    ///
[265](https://docs.rs#265)    /// # Examples
[266](https://docs.rs#266)    ///
[267](https://docs.rs#267)    /// See [`is_mime`](./fn.is_mime.html).
[268](https://docs.rs#268)    pub fn is_mime(&self, buf: &[u8], mime_type: &str) -> bool {
[269](https://docs.rs#269)        self.iter_matchers()
[270](https://docs.rs#270)            .any(|kind| kind.mime_type() == mime_type && kind.matches(buf))
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    }
[272](https://docs.rs#272)
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    /// Returns whether an extension is supported.
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    ///
[275](https://docs.rs#275)    /// # Examples
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    ///
[277](https://docs.rs#277)    /// See [`is_supported`](./fn.is_supported.html).
[278](https://docs.rs#278)    pub fn is_supported(&self, extension: &str) -> bool {
[279](https://docs.rs#279)        self.iter_matchers()
[280](https://docs.rs#280)            .any(|kind| kind.extension() == extension)
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    }
[282](https://docs.rs#282)
[283](https://docs.rs#283)    /// Returns whether a mime type is supported.
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    ///
[285](https://docs.rs#285)    /// # Examples
[286](https://docs.rs#286)    ///
[287](https://docs.rs#287)    /// See [`is_mime_supported`](./fn.is_mime_supported.html).
[288](https://docs.rs#288)    pub fn is_mime_supported(&self, mime_type: &str) -> bool {
[289](https://docs.rs#289)        self.iter_matchers()
[290](https://docs.rs#290)            .any(|kind| kind.mime_type() == mime_type)
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    }
[292](https://docs.rs#292)
[293](https://docs.rs#293)    /// Determines whether a buffer is an application type.
[294](https://docs.rs#294)    ///
[295](https://docs.rs#295)    /// # Examples

[368](https://docs.rs#368)    ///
[369](https://docs.rs#369)    /// ```rust
[370](https://docs.rs#370)    /// # #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[371](https://docs.rs#371)    /// # fn run() {
[372](https://docs.rs#372)    /// fn custom_matcher(buf: &[u8]) -> bool {
[373](https://docs.rs#373)    ///     return buf.len() >= 3 && buf[0] == 0x10 && buf[1] == 0x11 && buf[2] == 0x12;
[374](https://docs.rs#374)    /// }
[375](https://docs.rs#375)    ///
[376](https://docs.rs#376)    /// let mut info = infer::Infer::new();
[377](https://docs.rs#377)    /// info.add("custom/foo", "foo", custom_matcher);
[378](https://docs.rs#378)    /// let buf = [0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13];
[379](https://docs.rs#379)    /// assert!(info.is_custom(&buf));
[380](https://docs.rs#380)    /// # }
[381](https://docs.rs#381)    /// ```
[382](https://docs.rs#382)    pub fn is_custom(&self, buf: &[u8]) -> bool {

[384](https://docs.rs#384)    }
[385](https://docs.rs#385)
[386](https://docs.rs#386)    /// Adds a custom matcher.
[387](https://docs.rs#387)    ///
[388](https://docs.rs#388)    /// Custom matchers are matched in order of addition and before
[389](https://docs.rs#389)    /// the default set of matchers.
[390](https://docs.rs#390)    ///
[391](https://docs.rs#391)    /// # Examples
[392](https://docs.rs#392)    ///
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    /// ```rust
[394](https://docs.rs#394)    /// fn custom_matcher(buf: &[u8]) -> bool {
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    ///     return buf.len() >= 3 && buf[0] == 0x10 && buf[1] == 0x11 && buf[2] == 0x12;
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    /// }
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    ///
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    /// let mut info = infer::Infer::new();
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    /// info.add("custom/foo", "foo", custom_matcher);
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    /// let buf = [0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13];
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    /// let kind =  info.get(&buf).expect("file type is known");
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    ///
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    /// assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "custom/foo");
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    /// assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "foo");
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    /// ```
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    pub fn add(&mut self, mime_type: &'static str, extension: &'static str, m: Matcher) {
[408](https://docs.rs#408)        self.mmap.push(Type::new_static(
[409](https://docs.rs#409)            MatcherType::Custom,
[410](https://docs.rs#410)            mime_type,
[411](https://docs.rs#411)            extension,
[412](https://docs.rs#412)            WrapMatcher(m),
[413](https://docs.rs#413)        ));
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    }
[415](https://docs.rs#415)
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    fn is_type(&self, buf: &[u8], matcher_type: MatcherType) -> bool {
[417](https://docs.rs#417)        self.iter_matchers()
[418](https://docs.rs#418)            .any(|kind| kind.matcher_type() == matcher_type && kind.matches(buf))
[419](https://docs.rs#419)    }
[420](https://docs.rs#420)}

[609](https://docs.rs#609)#[cfg(test)]
[610](https://docs.rs#610)mod tests {
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    use super::Infer;
[613](https://docs.rs#613)
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    #[test]
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    fn test_get_unknown() {
[616](https://docs.rs#616)        let buf = [];
[617](https://docs.rs#617)        assert!(crate::get(&buf).is_none());
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    }
[619](https://docs.rs#619)
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    #[test]
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    fn test_get_jpeg() {
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
[623](https://docs.rs#623)        let kind = crate::get(&buf).expect("file type is known");
[624](https://docs.rs#624)        assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "jpg");
[625](https://docs.rs#625)        assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "image/jpeg");
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    }
[627](https://docs.rs#627)
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    #[test]
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    fn test_matcher_type() {
[630](https://docs.rs#630)        let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
[631](https://docs.rs#631)        let kind = crate::get(&buf).expect("file type is known");
[632](https://docs.rs#632)        assert_eq!(kind.matcher_type(), crate::MatcherType::Image);
[633](https://docs.rs#633)    }
[634](https://docs.rs#634)
[635](https://docs.rs#635)    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[636](https://docs.rs#636)    #[test]
[637](https://docs.rs#637)    fn test_custom_matcher_ordering() {
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        // overrides jpeg matcher
[639](https://docs.rs#639)        fn foo_matcher(buf: &[u8]) -> bool {
[640](https://docs.rs#640)            buf.len() > 2 && buf[0] == 0xFF && buf[1] == 0xD8 && buf[2] == 0xFF
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        }
[642](https://docs.rs#642)
[643](https://docs.rs#643)        // overrides png matcher
[644](https://docs.rs#644)        fn bar_matcher(buf: &[u8]) -> bool {
[645](https://docs.rs#645)            buf.len() > 3 && buf[0] == 0x89 && buf[1] == 0x50 && buf[2] == 0x4E && buf[3] == 0x47
[646](https://docs.rs#646)        }
[647](https://docs.rs#647)
[648](https://docs.rs#648)        let mut info = Infer::new();
[649](https://docs.rs#649)        info.add("custom/foo", "foo", foo_matcher);
[650](https://docs.rs#650)        info.add("custom/bar", "bar", bar_matcher);
[651](https://docs.rs#651)
[652](https://docs.rs#652)        let buf_foo = &[0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF];
[653](https://docs.rs#653)        let typ = info.get(buf_foo).expect("type is matched");
[654](https://docs.rs#654)        assert_eq!(typ.mime_type(), "custom/foo");
[655](https://docs.rs#655)        assert_eq!(typ.extension(), "foo");
[656](https://docs.rs#656)
[657](https://docs.rs#657)        let buf_bar = &[0x89, 0x50, 0x4E, 0x47];
[658](https://docs.rs#658)        let typ = info.get(buf_bar).expect("type is matched");
[659](https://docs.rs#659)        assert_eq!(typ.mime_type(), "custom/bar");
[660](https://docs.rs#660)        assert_eq!(typ.extension(), "bar");
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    }
[662](https://docs.rs#662)}

# infer::app - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/infer/0.19.0/infer/app/index.html

## Expand description

All the supported matchers categorized and exposed as functions

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [is_coff](https://docs.rs/fn.is_coff.html)
- Returns whether a buffer is a Common Object File Format.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_coff_i386.html)- coff_ - i386
- Returns whether a buffer is a Common Object File Format for i386 architecture.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_coff_ia64.html)- coff_ - ia64
- Returns whether a buffer is a Common Object File Format for Itanium architecture.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_coff_x64.html)- coff_ - x64
- Returns whether a buffer is a Common Object File Format for x64 architecture.
- [is_der](https://docs.rs/fn.is_der.html)
- Returns whether a buffer DER encoded X.509 certificate.
- [is_dex](https://docs.rs/fn.is_dex.html)
- Returns whether a buffer is a Dalvik Executable (DEX).
- [is_dey](https://docs.rs/fn.is_dey.html)
- Returns whether a buffer is a Dey Optimized Dalvik Executable (ODEX).
- [is_dll](https://docs.rs/fn.is_dll.html)
- Returns whether a buffer is a DLL. DLL and EXE have the same magic number, so returns true also for an EXE.
- [is_elf](https://docs.rs/fn.is_elf.html)
- Returns whether a buffer is an ELF.
- [is_exe](https://docs.rs/fn.is_exe.html)
- Returns whether a buffer is an EXE. DLL and EXE have the same magic number, so returns true also for a DLL.
- [is_java](https://docs.rs/fn.is_java.html)
- Returns whether a buffer is compiled Java bytecode.
- [is_llvm](https://docs.rs/fn.is_llvm.html)
- Returns whether a buffer is LLVM Bitcode.
- [is_mach](https://docs.rs/fn.is_mach.html)
- Returns whether a buffer is a Mach-O binary.
- [is_pem](https://docs.rs/fn.is_pem.html)
- Returns whether a buffer is pem
- [is_wasm](https://docs.rs/fn.is_wasm.html)
- Returns whether a buffer is a wasm.

# Infer in infer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/infer/0.19.0/infer/struct.Infer.html

`pub struct Infer { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Infer allows to use a custom set of `Matcher`s for infering a MIME type.

Most operations can be done by using the *top level functions*, but when custom matchers
are needed every call has to go through the `Infer` struct to be able
to see the custom matchers.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Returns the file type of the buffer.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let info = infer::Infer::new();
let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
let kind = info.get(&buf).expect("file type is known");
assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "image/jpeg");
assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "jpg");
```
Determines whether a buffer is one of the custom types added.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-14)Examples

```
fn custom_matcher(buf: &[u8]) -> bool {
    return buf.len() >= 3 && buf[0] == 0x10 && buf[1] == 0x11 && buf[2] == 0x12;
}
let mut info = infer::Infer::new();
info.add("custom/foo", "foo", custom_matcher);
let buf = [0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13];
assert!(info.is_custom(&buf));
```
Adds a custom matcher.

Custom matchers are matched in order of addition and before the default set of matchers.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-15)Examples

```
fn custom_matcher(buf: &[u8]) -> bool {
    return buf.len() >= 3 && buf[0] == 0x10 && buf[1] == 0x11 && buf[2] == 0x12;
}
let mut info = infer::Infer::new();
info.add("custom/foo", "foo", custom_matcher);
let buf = [0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13];
let kind =  info.get(&buf).expect("file type is known");
assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "custom/foo");
assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "foo");
```
## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#synthetic-implementations)

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```

Returns the mime type

```
4fn main() {
5    let mut args = args();
6    let path = match args.nth(1) {
7        Some(path) => path,
8        None => {
9            eprintln!("Please specify the file path");
10            exit(1);
11        }
12    };
13
14    match infer::get_from_path(path) {
15        Ok(Some(info)) => {
16            println!("Through the arcane magic of this crate we determined the file type to be");
17            println!("mime type: {}", info.mime_type());
18            println!("extension: {}", info.extension());
19        }
20        Ok(None) => {
21            eprintln!("Unknown file type 😞");
22            eprintln!("If you think infer should be able to recognize this file type open an issue on GitHub!");
23            exit(1);
24        }
25        Err(e) => {
26            eprintln!("Looks like something went wrong 😔");
27            eprintln!("{}", e);
28            exit(1);
29        }
30    }
31}
```

# get_from_path in infer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/infer/0.19.0/infer/fn.get_from_path.html

## Expand description

Returns the file type of the file given a path.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns an error if we fail to read the path.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let kind = infer::get_from_path("testdata/sample.jpg")
    .expect("file read successfully")
    .expect("file type is known");
assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "image/jpeg");
assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "jpg");
```
```
4fn main() {
5    let mut args = args();
6    let path = match args.nth(1) {
7        Some(path) => path,
8        None => {
9            eprintln!("Please specify the file path");
10            exit(1);
11        }
12    };
13
14    match infer::get_from_path(path) {
15        Ok(Some(info)) => {
16            println!("Through the arcane magic of this crate we determined the file type to be");
17            println!("mime type: {}", info.mime_type());
18            println!("extension: {}", info.extension());
19        }
20        Ok(None) => {
21            eprintln!("Unknown file type 😞");
22            eprintln!("If you think infer should be able to recognize this file type open an issue on GitHub!");
23            exit(1);
24        }
25        Err(e) => {
26            eprintln!("Looks like something went wrong 😔");
27            eprintln!("{}", e);
28            exit(1);
29        }
30    }
31}
```

# is in infer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/infer/0.19.0/infer/fn.is.html

# Function is

[Source](../src/infer/lib.rs.html#475-477) `pub fn is(buf: &[`[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)], extension: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

## Expand description

Determines whether a buffer is of given extension.

[§](#examples)Examples

```
let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
assert!(infer::is(&buf, "jpg"));
```

# infer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/infer/latest/infer/

## Expand description

Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#get-the-type-of-a-buffer)Get the type of a buffer

```
let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
let kind = infer::get(&buf).expect("file type is known");
assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "image/jpeg");
assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "jpg");
assert_eq!(kind.matcher_type(), infer::MatcherType::Image);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#check-file-type-by-path)Check file type by path

```
let kind = infer::get_from_path("testdata/sample.jpg")
    .expect("file read successfully")
    .expect("file type is known");
assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "image/jpeg");
assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "jpg");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#check-for-specific-type)Check for specific type

```
let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
assert!(infer::image::is_jpeg(&buf));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#check-for-specific-type-class)Check for specific type class

```
let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
assert!(infer::is_image(&buf));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#adds-a-custom-file-type-matcher)Adds a custom file type matcher

Here we actually need to use the `Infer` struct to be able to declare custom matchers.

```
fn custom_matcher(buf: &[u8]) -> bool {
    return buf.len() >= 3 && buf[0] == 0x10 && buf[1] == 0x11 && buf[2] == 0x12;
}
let mut info = infer::Infer::new();
info.add("custom/foo", "foo", custom_matcher);
let buf = [0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13];
let kind = info.get(&buf).unwrap();
assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "custom/foo");
assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "foo");
```

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/infer/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

A Rust library for reading/writing [Compound File Binary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compound_File_Binary_Format) (structured storage)
files.  See [MS-CFB](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/dd942138.aspx)
for the format specification.

# infer 0.18.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/infer/0.18.0

# infer

Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.

Adaptation of [filetype](https://github.com/h2non/filetype) Go package ported to Rust.

Does not require magic file database (i.e. `/etc/magic`).

## Features

- Supports a [wide range](https://docs.rs#supported-types)of file types
- Provides file extension and MIME type
- File discovery by extension or MIME type
- File discovery by class (image, video, audio...)
- Supports custom new types and matchers

## Installation

This crate works with Cargo and is on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/infer).
Add it to your `Cargo.toml` like so:

```
[]
 = "0.3"
```
If you are not using the custom matcher or the file type from file path functionality you can make this crate even lighter by importing it with no default features, like so:

```
[]
 = {  = "0.3",  = false }
```
## no_std and no_alloc support

This crate supports `no_std` and `no_alloc` environments. `std` support is enabled by default,
but you can disable it by importing the crate with no default features, making it depend
only on the Rust `core` Library.

`alloc` has to be enabled to be able to use custom file matchers.

`std` has to be enabled to be able to get the file type from a file given the file path.

## Examples

Most operations can be done via *top level functions*, but they are also available through the `Infer`
struct, which must be used when dealing custom matchers.

### Get the type of a buffer

```
let buf = ;
let kind = get.expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check file type by path

```
let kind = get_from_path
    .expect
    .expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check for specific type

```
let buf = ;
assert!;
```
### Check for specific type class

```
let buf = ;
assert!;
```
### Adds a custom file type matcher

```
let mut info = new;
info.add;
let buf = ;
let kind = info.get.expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
## Supported types

#### Image

- **jpg**-- `image/jpeg`
- **png**-- `image/png`
- **gif**-- `image/gif`
- **webp**-- `image/webp`
- **cr2**-- `image/x-canon-cr2`
- **tif**-- `image/tiff`
- **bmp**-- `image/bmp`
- **heif**-- `image/heif`
- **avif**-- `image/avif`
- **jxr**-- `image/vnd.ms-photo`
- **psd**-- `image/vnd.adobe.photoshop`
- **ico**-- `image/vnd.microsoft.icon`
- **ora**-- `image/openraster`
- **djvu**-- `image/vnd.djvu`

#### Video

- **mp4**-- `video/mp4`
- **m4v**-- `video/x-m4v`
- **mkv**-- `video/x-matroska`
- **webm**-- `video/webm`
- **mov**-- `video/quicktime`
- **avi**-- `video/x-msvideo`
- **wmv**-- `video/x-ms-wmv`
- **mpg**-- `video/mpeg`
- **flv**-- `video/x-flv`

#### Audio

- **mid**-- `audio/midi`
- **mp3**-- `audio/mpeg`
- **m4a**-- `audio/m4a`
- **ogg**-- `audio/ogg`
- **flac**-- `audio/x-flac`
- **wav**-- `audio/x-wav`
- **amr**-- `audio/amr`
- **aac**-- `audio/aac`
- **aiff**-- `audio/x-aiff`
- **dsf**-- `audio/x-dsf`
- **ape**-- `audio/x-ape`

#### Archive

- **epub**-- `application/epub+zip`
- **zip**-- `application/zip`
- **tar**-- `application/x-tar`
- **rar**-- `application/vnd.rar`
- **gz**-- `application/gzip`
- **bz2**-- `application/x-bzip2`
- **bz3**-- `application/vnd.bzip3`
- **7z**-- `application/x-7z-compressed`
- **xz**-- `application/x-xz`
- **pdf**-- `application/pdf`
- **swf**-- `application/x-shockwave-flash`
- **rtf**-- `application/rtf`
- **eot**-- `application/octet-stream`
- **ps**-- `application/postscript`
- **sqlite**-- `application/vnd.sqlite3`
- **nes**-- `application/x-nintendo-nes-rom`
- **crx**-- `application/x-google-chrome-extension`
- **cab**-- `application/vnd.ms-cab-compressed`
- **deb**-- `application/vnd.debian.binary-package`
- **ar**-- `application/x-unix-archive`
- **Z**-- `application/x-compress`
- **lz**-- `application/x-lzip`
- **rpm**-- `application/x-rpm`
- **dcm**-- `application/dicom`
- **zst**-- `application/zstd`
- **lz4**-- `application/x-lz4`
- **msi**-- `application/x-ole-storage`
- **cpio**-- `application/x-cpio`

#### Book

- **epub**-- `application/epub+zip`
- **mobi**-- `application/x-mobipocket-ebook`

#### Documents

- **doc**-- `application/msword`
- **docx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`
- **xls**-- `application/vnd.ms-excel`
- **xlsx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`
- **ppt**-- `application/vnd.ms-powerpoint`
- **pptx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation`
- **odt**-- `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text`
- **ods**-- `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet`
- **odp**-- `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation`

#### Font

- **woff**-- `application/font-woff`
- **woff2**-- `application/font-woff`
- **ttf**-- `application/font-sfnt`
- **otf**-- `application/font-sfnt`

#### Application

- **wasm**-- `application/wasm`
- **exe**-- `application/vnd.microsoft.portable-executable`
- **dll**-- `application/vnd.microsoft.portable-executable`
- **elf**-- `application/x-executable`
- **bc**-- `application/llvm`
- **mach**-- `application/x-mach-binary`
- **class**-- `application/java`
- **dex**-- `application/vnd.android.dex`
- **dey**-- `application/vnd.android.dey`
- **der**-- `application/x-x509-ca-cert`
- **obj**-- `application/x-executable`

## Known Issues

- `exe`and- `dll`have the same magic number so it's not possible to tell which one just based on the binary data.- `exe`is returned for all.

MIT

# infer 0.16.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/infer/0.16.0

# infer

Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.

Adaptation of [filetype](https://github.com/h2non/filetype) Go package ported to Rust.

Does not require magic file database (i.e. `/etc/magic`).

## Features

- Supports a [wide range](https://docs.rs#supported-types)of file types
- Provides file extension and MIME type
- File discovery by extension or MIME type
- File discovery by class (image, video, audio...)
- Supports custom new types and matchers

## Installation

This crate works with Cargo and is on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/infer).
Add it to your `Cargo.toml` like so:

```
[]
 = "0.3"
```
If you are not using the custom matcher or the file type from file path functionality you can make this crate even lighter by importing it with no default features, like so:

```
[]
 = {  = "0.3",  = false }
```
## no_std and no_alloc support

This crate supports `no_std` and `no_alloc` environments. `std` support is enabled by default,
but you can disable it by importing the crate with no default features, making it depend
only on the Rust `core` Library.

`alloc` has to be enabled to be able to use custom file matchers.

`std` has to be enabled to be able to get the file type from a file given the file path.

## Examples

Most operations can be done via *top level functions*, but they are also available through the `Infer`
struct, which must be used when dealing custom matchers.

### Get the type of a buffer

```
let buf = ;
let kind = get.expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check file type by path

```
let kind = get_from_path
    .expect
    .expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check for specific type

```
let buf = ;
assert!;
```
### Check for specific type class

```
let buf = ;
assert!;
```
### Adds a custom file type matcher

```
let mut info = new;
info.add;
let buf = ;
let kind = info.get.expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```

# infer 0.12.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/infer/0.12.0

# infer

Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.

Adaptation of [filetype](https://github.com/h2non/filetype) Go package ported to Rust.

Does not require magic file database (i.e. `/etc/magic`).

## Features

- Supports a [wide range](https://docs.rs#supported-types)of file types
- Provides file extension and MIME type
- File discovery by extension or MIME type
- File discovery by class (image, video, audio...)
- Supports custom new types and matchers

## Installation

This crate works with Cargo and is on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/infer).
Add it to your `Cargo.toml` like so:

```
[]
 = "0.3"
```
If you are not using the custom matcher or the file type from file path functionality you can make this crate even lighter by importing it with no default features, like so:

```
[]
 = {  = "0.3",  = false }
```
## no_std and no_alloc support

This crate supports `no_std` and `no_alloc` environments. `std` support is enabled by default,
but you can disable it by importing the crate with no default features, making it depend
only on the Rust `core` Library.

`alloc` has to be enabled to be able to use custom file matchers.

`std` has to be enabled to be able to get the file type from a file given the file path.

## Examples

Most operations can be done via *top level functions*, but they are also available through the `Infer`
struct, which must be used when dealing custom matchers.

### Get the type of a buffer

```
let buf = ;
let kind = get.expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check file type by path

```
let kind = get_from_path
    .expect
    .expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check for specific type

```
let buf = ;
assert!;
```
### Check for specific type class

```
let buf = ;
assert!;
```
### Adds a custom file type matcher

```
let mut info = new;
info.add;
let buf = ;
let kind = info.get.expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
## Supported types

#### Image

- **avi**-- `video/x-msvideo`

assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
## Supported types

#### Image

- **jpg**-- `image/jpeg`
- **png**-- `image/png`
- **gif**-- `image/gif`
- **webp**-- `image/webp`
- **cr2**-- `image/x-canon-cr2`
- **tif**-- `image/tiff`
- **bmp**-- `image/bmp`
- **heif**-- `image/heif`
- **avif**-- `image/avif`
- **jxr**-- `image/vnd.ms-photo`
- **psd**-- `image/vnd.adobe.photoshop`
- **ico**-- `image/vnd.microsoft.icon`

#### Video

- **mp4**-- `video/mp4`
- **m4v**-- `video/x-m4v`
- **mkv**-- `video/x-matroska`
- **webm**-- `video/webm`
- **mov**-- `video/quicktime`
- **avi**-- `video/x-msvideo`
- **wmv**-- `video/x-ms-wmv`
- **mpg**-- `video/mpeg`
- **flv**-- `video/x-flv`

#### Audio

- **mid**-- `audio/midi`
- **mp3**-- `audio/mpeg`
- **m4a**-- `audio/m4a`
- **ogg**-- `audio/ogg`
- **flac**-- `audio/x-flac`
- **wav**-- `audio/x-wav`
- **amr**-- `audio/amr`
- **aac**-- `audio/aac`
- **aiff**-- `audio/x-aiff`
- **dsf**-- `audio/x-dsf`
- **ape**-- `audio/x-ape`

#### Archive

- **epub**-- `application/epub+zip`
- **zip**-- `application/zip`
- **tar**-- `application/x-tar`
- **rar**-- `application/vnd.rar`
- **gz**-- `application/gzip`
- **bz2**-- `application/x-bzip2`
- **7z**-- `application/x-7z-compressed`
- **xz**-- `application/x-xz`
- **pdf**-- `application/pdf`
- **swf**-- `application/x-shockwave-flash`
- **rtf**-- `application/rtf`
- **eot**-- `application/octet-stream`
- **ps**-- `application/postscript`
- **sqlite**-- `application/vnd.sqlite3`
- **nes**-- `application/x-nintendo-nes-rom`
- **crx**-- `application/x-google-chrome-extension`
- **cab**-- `application/vnd.ms-cab-compressed`
- **deb**-- `application/vnd.debian.binary-package`
- **ar**-- `application/x-unix-archive`
- **Z**-- `application/x-compress`
- **lz**-- `application/x-lzip`
- **rpm**-- `application/x-rpm`
- **dcm**-- `application/dicom`
- **zst**-- `application/zstd`
- **msi**-- `application/x-ole-storage`

#### Book

- **epub**-- `application/epub+zip`
- **mobi**-- `application/x-mobipocket-ebook`

#### Documents

- **doc**-- `application/msword`
- **docx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`
- **xls**-- `application/vnd.ms-excel`
- **xlsx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`
- **ppt**-- `application/vnd.ms-powerpoint`
- **pptx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation`
- **odt**-- `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text`
- **ods**-- `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet`
- **odp**-- `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation`

- **woff2**-- `application/font-woff`
- **ttf**-- `application/font-sfnt`
- **otf**-- `application/font-sfnt`

#### Application

- **wasm**-- `application/wasm`
- **exe**-- `application/vnd.microsoft.portable-executable`
- **dll**-- `application/vnd.microsoft.portable-executable`
- **elf**-- `application/x-executable`
- **bc**-- `application/llvm`
- **mach**-- `application/x-mach-binary`
- **class**-- `application/java`
- **dex**-- `application/vnd.android.dex`
- **dey**-- `application/vnd.android.dey`
- **der**-- `application/x-x509-ca-cert`
- **obj**-- `application/x-executable`

## Known Issues

- `exe`and- `dll`have the same magic number so it's not possible to tell which one just based on the binary data.- `exe`is returned for all.

# infer 0.8.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/infer/0.8.1

# infer

Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.

Adaptation of [filetype](https://github.com/h2non/filetype) Go package ported to Rust.

Does not require magic file database (i.e. `/etc/magic`).

## Features

- Supports a [wide range](https://docs.rs#supported-types)of file types
- Provides file extension and MIME type
- File discovery by extension or MIME type
- File discovery by class (image, video, audio...)
- Supports custom new types and matchers

## Installation

This crate works with Cargo and is on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/infer).
Add it to your `Cargo.toml` like so:

```
[]
 = "0.3"
```
If you are not using the custom matcher or the file type from file path functionality you can make this crate even lighter by importing it with no default features, like so:

```
[]
 = {  = "0.3",  = false }
```
## no_std and no_alloc support

This crate supports `no_std` and `no_alloc` environments. `std` support is enabled by default,
but you can disable it by importing the crate with no default features, making it depend
only on the Rust `core` Library.

`alloc` has to be enabled to be able to use custom file matchers.

`std` has to be enabled to be able to get the file type from a file given the file path.

## Examples

Most operations can be done via *top level functions*, but they are also available through the `Infer`
struct, which must be used when dealing custom matchers.

### Get the type of a buffer

```
let buf = ;
let kind = get.expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check file type by path

```
let kind = get_from_path
    .expect
    .expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check for specific type

```
let buf = ;
assert!;
```
### Check for specific type class

```
let buf = ;
assert!;
```
### Adds a custom file type matcher

```
let mut info = new;
info.add;
let buf = ;
let kind = info.get.expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
## Supported types

#### Image

- **jpg**-- `image/jpeg`
- **png**-- `image/png`
- **gif**-- `image/gif`
- **webp**-- `image/webp`
- **cr2**-- `image/x-canon-cr2`
- **tif**-- `image/tiff`
- **bmp**-- `image/bmp`
- **heif**-- `image/heif`
- **avif**-- `image/avif`
- **jxr**-- `image/vnd.ms-photo`
- **psd**-- `image/vnd.adobe.photoshop`
- **ico**-- `image/vnd.microsoft.icon`

#### Video

- **mp4**-- `video/mp4`
- **m4v**-- `video/x-m4v`
- **mkv**-- `video/x-matroska`
- **webm**-- `video/webm`
- **mov**-- `video/quicktime`
- **avi**-- `video/x-msvideo`
- **wmv**-- `video/x-ms-wmv`
- **mpg**-- `video/mpeg`
- **flv**-- `video/x-flv`

#### Audio

- **flac**-- `audio/x-flac`

- **ape**-- `audio/x-ape`

#### Archive

only on the Rust `core` Library.

`alloc` has to be enabled to be able to use custom file matchers.

`std` has to be enabled to be able to get the file type from a file given the file path.

## Examples

Most operations can be done via *top level functions*, but they are also available through the `Infer`
struct, which must be used when dealing custom matchers.

### Get the type of a buffer

```

let kind = get.expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check file type by path

```
let kind = get_from_path
    .expect
    .expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check for specific type

### Check for specific type class

```

assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;

- **amr**-- `audio/amr`
- **aac**-- `audio/aac`
- **aiff**-- `audio/x-aiff`

#### Archive

- **epub**-- `application/epub+zip`
- **zip**-- `application/zip`
- **tar**-- `application/x-tar`
- **rar**-- `application/vnd.rar`
- **gz**-- `application/gzip`
- **bz2**-- `application/x-bzip2`
- **7z**-- `application/x-7z-compressed`
- **xz**-- `application/x-xz`
- **pdf**-- `application/pdf`
- **swf**-- `application/x-shockwave-flash`
- **rtf**-- `application/rtf`
- **eot**-- `application/octet-stream`
- **ps**-- `application/postscript`
- **sqlite**-- `application/vnd.sqlite3`
- **nes**-- `application/x-nintendo-nes-rom`
- **crx**-- `application/x-google-chrome-extension`
- **cab**-- `application/vnd.ms-cab-compressed`
- **deb**-- `application/vnd.debian.binary-package`
- **ar**-- `application/x-unix-archive`
- **Z**-- `application/x-compress`
- **lz**-- `application/x-lzip`

- **dcm**-- `application/dicom`
- **zst**-- `application/zstd`
- **msi**-- `application/x-ole-storage`

#### Book

- **epub**-- `application/epub+zip`
- **mobi**-- `application/x-mobipocket-ebook`

#### Documents

- **doc**-- `application/msword`
- **docx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`
- **xls**-- `application/vnd.ms-excel`
- **xlsx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`
- **ppt**-- `application/vnd.ms-powerpoint`
- **pptx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation`
- **odt**-- `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text`
- **ods**-- `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet`
- **odp**-- `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation`

- **woff2**-- `application/font-woff`

- **otf**-- `application/font-sfnt`

- **dey**-- `application/vnd.android.dey`
- **der**-- `application/x-x509-ca-cert`
- **obj**-- `application/x-executable`

## Known Issues

- `exe`and- `dll`have the same magic number so it's not possible to tell which one just based on the binary data.- `exe`is returned for all.

# infer

Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.

Adaptation of [filetype](https://github.com/h2non/filetype) Go package ported to Rust.

Does not require magic file database (i.e. `/etc/magic`).

## Features

- Supports a [wide range](https://docs.rs#supported-types)of file types
- Provides file extension and MIME type
- File discovery by extension or MIME type
- File discovery by class (image, video, audio...)
- Supports custom new types and matchers

## Installation

This crate works with Cargo and is on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/infer).
Add it to your `Cargo.toml` like so:

```
[]

#### Image

- **png**-- `image/png`
- **gif**-- `image/gif`

- **cr2**-- `image/x-canon-cr2`
- **tif**-- `image/tiff`
- **bmp**-- `image/bmp`
- **heif**-- `image/heif`

- **ico**-- `image/vnd.microsoft.icon`

#### Video

- **mp4**-- `video/mp4`
- **m4v**-- `video/x-m4v`
- **mkv**-- `video/x-matroska`
- **webm**-- `video/webm`
- **mov**-- `video/quicktime`
- **avi**-- `video/x-msvideo`
- **wmv**-- `video/x-ms-wmv`
- **mpg**-- `video/mpeg`
- **flv**-- `video/x-flv`

#### Audio

- **mid**-- `audio/midi`
- **mp3**-- `audio/mpeg`
- **m4a**-- `audio/m4a`
- **ogg**-- `audio/ogg`
- **flac**-- `audio/x-flac`
- **wav**-- `audio/x-wav`
- **amr**-- `audio/amr`
- **aac**-- `audio/aac`

#### Archive

- **epub**-- `application/epub+zip`
- **zip**-- `application/zip`
- **tar**-- `application/x-tar`
- **rar**-- `application/vnd.rar`
- **gz**-- `application/gzip`
- **bz2**-- `application/x-bzip2`
- **7z**-- `application/x-7z-compressed`
- **xz**-- `application/x-xz`
- **pdf**-- `application/pdf`
- **swf**-- `application/x-shockwave-flash`
- **rtf**-- `application/rtf`
- **eot**-- `application/octet-stream`
- **ps**-- `application/postscript`
- **sqlite**-- `application/vnd.sqlite3`
- **nes**-- `application/x-nintendo-nes-rom`
- **crx**-- `application/x-google-chrome-extension`
- **cab**-- `application/vnd.ms-cab-compressed`
- **deb**-- `application/vnd.debian.binary-package`
- **ar**-- `application/x-unix-archive`
- **Z**-- `application/x-compress`
- **lz**-- `application/x-lzip`
- **rpm**-- `application/x-rpm`
- **dcm**-- `application/dicom`
- **zst**-- `application/zstd`
- **msi**-- `application/x-ole-storage`

#### Book

- **epub**-- `application/epub+zip`
- **mobi**-- `application/x-mobipocket-ebook`

#### Documents

- **doc**-- `application/msword`
- **docx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`
- **xls**-- `application/vnd.ms-excel`
- **xlsx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`
- **ppt**-- `application/vnd.ms-powerpoint`
- **pptx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation`

#### Font

- **woff**-- `application/font-woff`
- **woff2**-- `application/font-woff`
- **ttf**-- `application/font-sfnt`
- **otf**-- `application/font-sfnt`

#### Application

- **wasm**-- `application/wasm`
- **exe**-- `application/vnd.microsoft.portable-executable`
- **dll**-- `application/vnd.microsoft.portable-executable`
- **elf**-- `application/x-executable`
- **bc**-- `application/llvm`
- **mach**-- `application/x-mach-binary`
- **class**-- `application/java`
- **dex**-- `application/vnd.android.dex`
- **dey**-- `application/vnd.android.dey`
- **der**-- `application/x-x509-ca-cert`
- **obj**-- `application/x-executable`

## Known Issues

- `doc`,- `ppt`,- `xls`,- `msi`all have the same magic number so it's not possible to tell which one just based on the binary data.- `doc`is returned for all.
- `exe`and- `dll`have the same magic number so it's not possible to tell which one just based on the binary data.- `exe`is returned for all.

MIT

    .expect

assert_eq!;

# infer 0.3.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/infer/0.3.1

# infer

Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.

Adaptation of [filetype](https://github.com/h2non/filetype) Go package ported to Rust.

Does not require magic file database (i.e. `/etc/magic`).

## Features

- Supports a [wide range](https://docs.rs#supported-types)of file types
- Provides file extension and MIME type
- File discovery by extension or MIME type
- File discovery by class (image, video, audio...)
- Supports custom new types and matchers

## Installation

This crate works with Cargo and is on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/infer).
Add it to your `Cargo.toml` like so:

```
[]
 = "0.3"
```
If you are not using the custom matcher or the file type from file path functionality you can make this crate even lighter by importing it with no default features, like so:

```
[]
 = {  = "0.3",  = false }
```
## no_std and no_alloc support

This crate supports `no_std` and `no_alloc` environments. `std` support is enabled by default,
but you can disable it by importing the crate with no default features, making it depend
only on the Rust `core` Library.

`alloc` has to be enabled to be able to use custom file matchers.

`std` has to be enabled to be able to get the file type from a file given the file path.

## Examples

Most operations can be done via *top level functions*, but they are also available through the `Infer`
struct, which must be used when dealing custom matchers.

### Get the type of a buffer

```
let buf = ;
let kind = get.expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check file type by path

```
let kind = get_from_path
    .expect
    .expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check for specific type

```

assert!;
```
### Check for specific type class

```

assert!;
```
### Adds a custom file type matcher

```

info.add;
let buf = ;
let kind = info.get.expect;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```

# infer

Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.

Adaptation of [filetype](https://github.com/h2non/filetype) Go package ported to Rust.

## Features

- Supports custom new types and matchers

## Documentation

## Installation

[crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/infer). Add it to your `Cargo.toml`
like so:

```
[]
 = "0.2"
```
## Examples

### Get the type of a buffer

```
use Infer;
let v = vec!;
let info = new;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check path

```
use Infer;
let info = new;
let res = info.get_from_path;
assert!;
let o = res.unwrap;
assert!;
let typ = o.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check for specific type

```
let v = vec!;
assert!;
```
### Check for specific type class

Note individual matcher functions do not require init

```

let info = new;
assert!;
```

assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```

- **docx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`
- **xls**-- `application/vnd.ms-excel`
- **xlsx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`
- **ppt**-- `application/vnd.ms-powerpoint`
- **pptx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation`

#### Font

- **woff**-- `application/font-woff`
- **woff2**-- `application/font-woff`
- **ttf**-- `application/font-sfnt`
- **otf**-- `application/font-sfnt`

#### Application

- **wasm**-- `application/wasm`
- **exe**-- `application/vnd.microsoft.portable-executable`
- **elf**-- `application/x-executable`
- **bc**-- `application/llvm`
- **class**-- `application/java`

## Known Issues

- `doc`,- `ppt`,- `xls`all have the same magic number so it's not possible to tell which one just based on the binary data.- `doc`is returned for all.

## License

MIT

# infer

Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.

Adaptation of [filetype](https://github.com/h2non/filetype) Go package ported to Rust.

Does not require magic file database (i.e. `/etc/magic`).

## Features

- Supports a [wide range](https://docs.rs#supported-types)of file types
- Provides file extension and MIME type
- File discovery by extension or MIME type
- File discovery by class (image, video, audio...)
- Supports custom new types and matchers

## Documentation

## Installation

This crate works with Cargo and is on
[crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/infer). Add it to your `Cargo.toml`
like so:

```
[]
 = "0.2"
```
## Examples

### Get the type of a buffer

```
use Infer;
let v = vec!;
let info = new;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check path

```
use Infer;
let info = new;
let res = info.get_from_path;
assert!;
let o = res.unwrap;
assert!;
let typ = o.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check for specific type

```
let v = vec!;
assert!;
```
### Check for specific type class

Note individual matcher functions do not require init

```
let v = vec!;
let info = new;
assert!;
```
### Adds a custom file type matcher

```
let mut info = new;
info.add;
let v = vec!;
let res =  info.get.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```

- **gz**-- `application/gzip`
- **bz2**-- `application/x-bzip2`
- **7z**-- `application/x-7z-compressed`
- **xz**-- `application/x-xz`
- **pdf**-- `application/pdf`
- **swf**-- `application/x-shockwave-flash`
- **rtf**-- `application/rtf`
- **eot**-- `application/octet-stream`
- **ps**-- `application/postscript`
- **sqlite**-- `application/x-sqlite3`
- **nes**-- `application/x-nintendo-nes-rom`
- **crx**-- `application/x-google-chrome-extension`
- **cab**-- `application/vnd.ms-cab-compressed`
- **deb**-- `application/x-deb`
- **ar**-- `application/x-unix-archive`
- **Z**-- `application/x-compress`
- **lz**-- `application/x-lzip`
- **rpm**-- `application/x-rpm`
- **dcm**-- `application/dicom`
- **zst**-- `application/zstd`

#### Documents

- **doc**-- `application/msword`
- **docx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`
- **xls**-- `application/vnd.ms-excel`
- **xlsx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`
- **ppt**-- `application/vnd.ms-powerpoint`
- **pptx**-- `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation`

#### Font

- **woff**-- `application/font-woff`
- **woff2**-- `application/font-woff`
- **ttf**-- `application/font-sfnt`
- **otf**-- `application/font-sfnt`

#### Application

- **wasm**-- `application/wasm`
- **exe**-- `application/x-msdownload`
- **elf**-- `application/x-executable`
- **bc**-- `application/llvm`
- **class**-- `application/java`

## Known Issues

- `doc`,- `ppt`,- `xls`all have the same magic number so it's not possible to tell which one just based on the binary data.- `doc`is returned for all.

## License

MIT

# infer 0.1.4 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/infer/0.1.4

# infer

Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.

Adaptation of [filetype](https://github.com/h2non/filetype) Go package ported to Rust.

Does not require magic file database (i.e. `/etc/magic`).

## Features

- Supports a [wide range](https://docs.rs#supported-types)of file types
- Provides file extension and MIME type
- File discovery by extension or MIME type
- File discovery by class (image, video, audio...)
- Supports custom new types and matchers

## Documentation

## Installation

This crate works with Cargo and is on
[crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/infer). Add it to your `Cargo.toml`
like so:

```
[]
 = "0.1"
```
## Examples

### Get the type of a buffer

```
use Infer;
let v = vec!;
let info = new;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check path

```
use Infer;
let info = new;
let res = info.get_from_path;
assert!;
let o = res.unwrap;
assert!;
let typ = o.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Check for specific type

```
let v = vec!;
assert!;
```
### Check for specific type class

Note individual matcher functions do not require init

```
let v = vec!;
let info = new;
assert!;
```
### Adds a custom file type matcher

```
let mut info = new;
info.add;
let v = vec!;
let res =  info.get.unwrap;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
## Supported types

## Known Issues

- `doc`,- `ppt`,- `xls`all have the same magic number so it's not possible to tell which one just based on the binary data.- `doc`is returned for all.

# infer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/infer

## Expand description

Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#get-the-type-of-a-buffer)Get the type of a buffer

```
let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
let kind = infer::get(&buf).expect("file type is known");
assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "image/jpeg");
assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "jpg");
assert_eq!(kind.matcher_type(), infer::MatcherType::Image);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#check-file-type-by-path)Check file type by path

```
let kind = infer::get_from_path("testdata/sample.jpg")
    .expect("file read successfully")
    .expect("file type is known");
assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "image/jpeg");
assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "jpg");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#check-for-specific-type)Check for specific type

```
let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
assert!(infer::image::is_jpeg(&buf));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#check-for-specific-type-class)Check for specific type class

```
let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
assert!(infer::is_image(&buf));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#adds-a-custom-file-type-matcher)Adds a custom file type matcher

Here we actually need to use the `Infer` struct to be able to declare custom matchers.

```
fn custom_matcher(buf: &[u8]) -> bool {
    return buf.len() >= 3 && buf[0] == 0x10 && buf[1] == 0x11 && buf[2] == 0x12;
}
let mut info = infer::Infer::new();
info.add("custom/foo", "foo", custom_matcher);
let buf = [0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13];
let kind = info.get(&buf).unwrap();
assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "custom/foo");
assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "foo");
```

# infer 0.19.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/infer/latest/source/README.md

```
![Build Status](https://github.com/bojand/infer/workflows/build/badge.svg)
[![crates version](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/infer.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/infer)
[![documentation](https://docs.rs/infer/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/infer)
Small crate to infer file and MIME type by checking the
[magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)) signature.
Adaptation of [filetype](https://github.com/h2non/filetype) Go package ported to Rust.
Does not require magic file database (i.e. `/etc/magic`).
- ----
This crate works with Cargo and is on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/infer).
Add it to your `Cargo.toml` like so:
```toml
[dependencies]
infer = "0.3"
```
If you are not using the custom matcher or the file type from file path functionality you
can make this crate even lighter by importing it with no default features, like so:
```toml
[dependencies]
infer = { version = "0.3", default-features = false }
```
This crate supports `no_std` and `no_alloc` environments. `std` support is enabled by default,
but you can disable it by importing the crate with no default features, making it depend
only on the Rust `core` Library.
`alloc` has to be enabled to be able to use custom file matchers.
`std` has to be enabled to be able to get the file type from a file given the file path.
Most operations can be done via _top level functions_, but they are also available through the `Infer`
struct, which must be used when dealing custom matchers.
```rust
let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
let kind = infer::get(&buf).expect("file type is known");
assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "image/jpeg");
assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "jpg");
```
```rust
let kind = infer::get_from_path("testdata/sample.jpg")
assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "image/jpeg");
assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "jpg");
```
```rust
let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
assert!(infer::image::is_jpeg(&buf));
```
```rust
let buf = [0xFF, 0xD8, 0xFF, 0xAA];
assert!(infer::is_image(&buf));
```
```rust
fn custom_matcher(buf: &[u8]) -> bool {
}
let mut info = infer::Infer::new();
info.add("custom/foo", "foo", custom_matcher);
let buf = [0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13];
let kind = info.get(&buf).expect("file type is known");
assert_eq!(kind.mime_type(), "custom/foo");
assert_eq!(kind.extension(), "foo");
```
- -------------
- --------
- ----------
- ----------------------------
- -
- --------
- ---
- ----------
-
MIT
```

# byteorder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/byteorder/^1/

## Expand description

This crate provides convenience methods for encoding and decoding numbers in
either [big-endian or little-endian order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endianness).

The organization of the crate is pretty simple. A trait, [ ByteOrder](https://docs.rs/trait.ByteOrder.html), specifies
byte conversion methods for each type of number in Rust (sans numbers that have
a platform dependent size like

`usize` and `isize`). Two types, [and](https://docs.rs/enum.BigEndian.html)

`BigEndian`[implement these methods. Finally,](https://docs.rs/enum.LittleEndian.html)

`LittleEndian`[and](https://docs.rs/trait.ReadBytesExt.html)

`ReadBytesExt`[provide convenience methods available to all types that implement](https://docs.rs/trait.WriteBytesExt.html)

`WriteBytesExt`[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/trait.Read.html)

`Read`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/trait.Write.html)

`Write`An alias, [ NetworkEndian](https://docs.rs/type.NetworkEndian.html), for

[is provided to help improve code clarity.](https://docs.rs/enum.BigEndian.html)

`BigEndian`An additional alias, [ NativeEndian](https://docs.rs/type.NativeEndian.html), is provided for the endianness of the
local platform. This is convenient when serializing data for use and
conversions are not desired.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Read unsigned 16 bit big-endian integers from a [ Read](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/trait.Read.html) type:

```
use std::io::Cursor;
use byteorder::{BigEndian, ReadBytesExt};
let mut rdr = Cursor::new(vec![2, 5, 3, 0]);
// Note that we use type parameters to indicate which kind of byte order
// we want!
assert_eq!(517, rdr.read_u16::<BigEndian>().unwrap());
assert_eq!(768, rdr.read_u16::<BigEndian>().unwrap());
```
Write unsigned 16 bit little-endian integers to a [ Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/trait.Write.html) type:

```
use byteorder::{LittleEndian, WriteBytesExt};
let mut wtr = vec![];
wtr.write_u16::<LittleEndian>(517).unwrap();
wtr.write_u16::<LittleEndian>(768).unwrap();
assert_eq!(wtr, vec![5, 2, 0, 3]);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional Features

This crate optionally provides support for 128 bit values (`i128` and `u128`)
when built with the `i128` feature enabled.

This crate can also be used without the standard library.

[§](https://docs.rs#alternatives)Alternatives

Note that as of Rust 1.32, the standard numeric types provide built-in methods
like `to_le_bytes` and `from_le_bytes`, which support some of the same use
cases.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [BigEndian](https://docs.rs/enum.BigEndian.html)
- Defines big-endian serialization.
- [Little](https://docs.rs/enum.LittleEndian.html)- Endian
- Defines little-endian serialization.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Byte](https://docs.rs/trait.ByteOrder.html)- Order
- `ByteOrder`describes types that can serialize integers as bytes.
- [Read](https://docs.rs/trait.ReadBytesExt.html)- Bytes - Ext
- Extends `Read``std::io`.)
- [Write](https://docs.rs/trait.WriteBytesExt.html)- Bytes - Ext
- Extends `Write``std::io`.)

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [BE](https://docs.rs/type.BE.html)
- A type alias for `BigEndian`
- [LE](https://docs.rs/type.LE.html)
- A type alias for `LittleEndian`
- [Native](https://docs.rs/type.NativeEndian.html)- Endian
- Defines system native-endian serialization.
- [Network](https://docs.rs/type.NetworkEndian.html)- Endian
- Defines network byte order serialization.

# fnv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fnv/^1.0.7/

## Expand description

An implementation of the [Fowler–Noll–Vo hash function](http://www.isthe.com/chongo/tech/comp/fnv/index.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#about)About

The FNV hash function is a custom `Hasher` implementation that is more
efficient for smaller hash keys.

[The Rust FAQ states that](https://www.rust-lang.org/en-US/faq.html#why-are-rusts-hashmaps-slow) while the default `Hasher` implementation,
SipHash, is good in many cases, it is notably slower than other algorithms
with short keys, such as when you have a map of integers to other values.
In cases like these, [FNV is demonstrably faster](https://cglab.ca/~abeinges/blah/hash-rs/).

Its disadvantages are that it performs badly on larger inputs, and provides no protection against collision attacks, where a malicious user can craft specific keys designed to slow a hasher down. Thus, it is important to profile your program to ensure that you are using small hash keys, and be certain that your program could not be exposed to malicious inputs (including being a networked server).

The Rust compiler itself uses FNV, as it is not worried about denial-of-service attacks, and can assume that its inputs are going to be small—a perfect use case for FNV.

[§](https://docs.rs#using-fnv-in-a-hashmap)Using FNV in a `HashMap`

The `FnvHashMap` type alias is the easiest way to use the standard library’s
`HashMap` with FNV.

```
use fnv::FnvHashMap;
let mut map = FnvHashMap::default();
map.insert(1, "one");
map.insert(2, "two");
map = FnvHashMap::with_capacity_and_hasher(10, Default::default());
map.insert(1, "one");
map.insert(2, "two");
```
Note, the standard library’s `HashMap::new` and `HashMap::with_capacity`
are only implemented for the `RandomState` hasher, so using `Default` to
get the hasher is the next best option.

[§](https://docs.rs#using-fnv-in-a-hashset)Using FNV in a `HashSet`

Similarly, `FnvHashSet` is a type alias for the standard library’s `HashSet`
with FNV.

```
use fnv::FnvHashSet;
let mut set = FnvHashSet::default();
set.insert(1);
set.insert(2);
set = FnvHashSet::with_capacity_and_hasher(10, Default::default());
set.insert(1);
set.insert(2);
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [FnvHasher](https://docs.rs/struct.FnvHasher.html)
- An implementation of the Fowler–Noll–Vo hash function.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [FnvBuild](https://docs.rs/type.FnvBuildHasher.html)- Hasher
- A builder for default FNV hashers.
- [FnvHash](https://docs.rs/type.FnvHashMap.html)- Map
- A `HashMap`using a default FNV hasher.
- [FnvHash](https://docs.rs/type.FnvHashSet.html)- Set
- A `HashSet`using a default FNV hasher.

---

# uuid - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uuid/^1/

## Expand description

Generate and parse universally unique identifiers (UUIDs).

Here’s an example of a UUID:

`67e55044-10b1-426f-9247-bb680e5fe0c8`A UUID is a unique 128-bit value, stored as 16 octets, and regularly formatted as a hex string in five groups. UUIDs are used to assign unique identifiers to entities without requiring a central allocating authority.

They are particularly useful in distributed systems, though can be used in disparate areas, such as databases and network protocols. Typically a UUID is displayed in a readable string form as a sequence of hexadecimal digits, separated into groups by hyphens.

The uniqueness property is not strictly guaranteed, however for all practical purposes, it can be assumed that an unintentional collision would be extremely unlikely.

UUIDs have a number of standardized encodings that are specified in [RFC 9562](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc9562.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting started

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies.uuid]
version = "1.23.4"
# Lets you generate random UUIDs
features = [
    "v4",
]
```
When you want a UUID, you can generate one:

```
use uuid::Uuid;
let id = Uuid::new_v4();
```
If you have a UUID value, you can use its string literal form inline:

```
use uuid::{uuid, Uuid};
const ID: Uuid = uuid!("67e55044-10b1-426f-9247-bb680e5fe0c8");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#working-with-different-uuid-versions)Working with different UUID versions

This library supports all standardized methods for generating UUIDs through individual Cargo features.

By default, this crate depends on nothing but the Rust standard library and can parse and format UUIDs, but cannot generate them. Depending on the kind of UUID you’d like to work with, there are Cargo features that enable generating them:

- `v1`- Version 1 UUIDs using a timestamp and monotonic counter.
- `v3`- Version 3 UUIDs based on the MD5 hash of some data.
- `v4`- Version 4 UUIDs with random data.
- `v5`- Version 5 UUIDs based on the SHA1 hash of some data.
- `v6`- Version 6 UUIDs using a timestamp and monotonic counter.
- `v7`- Version 7 UUIDs using a Unix timestamp.
- `v8`- Version 8 UUIDs using user-defined data.

This library also includes a [ Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html) type that can be used to help construct UUIDs of any
version without any additional dependencies or features. It’s a lower-level API than

[that can be used when you need control over implicit requirements on things like a source of randomness.](https://docs.rs/struct.Uuid.html)

`Uuid`[§](https://docs.rs#which-uuid-version-should-i-use)Which UUID version should I use?

If you just want to generate unique identifiers then consider version 4 (`v4`) UUIDs. If you want
to use UUIDs as database keys or need to sort them then consider version 7 (`v7`) UUIDs.
Other versions should generally be avoided unless there’s an existing need for them.

Some UUID versions supersede others. Prefer version 6 over version 1 and version 5 over version 3.

[§](https://docs.rs#other-features)Other features

Other crate features can also be useful beyond the version support:

- `serde`- adds the ability to serialize and deserialize a UUID using- `serde`.
- `borsh`- adds the ability to serialize and deserialize a UUID using- `borsh`.
- `arbitrary`- adds an- `Arbitrary`trait implementation to- `Uuid`for fuzzing.
- `fast-rng`- uses a faster algorithm for generating random UUIDs when available. This feature requires more dependencies to compile, but is just as suitable for UUIDs as the default algorithm.
- `rng-rand`- forces- `rand`as the backend for randomness.
- `rng-getrandom`- forces- `getrandom`as the backend for randomness.
- `bytemuck`- adds a- `Pod`trait implementation to- `Uuid`for byte manipulation

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable features

Some features are unstable. They may be incomplete or depend on other unstable libraries. These include:

- `zerocopy`- adds support for zero-copy deserialization using the- `zerocopy`library.

Unstable features may break between minor releases.

To allow unstable features, you’ll need to enable the Cargo feature as
normal, but also pass an additional flag through your environment to opt-in
to unstable `uuid` features:

`RUSTFLAGS="--cfg uuid_unstable"`[§](https://docs.rs#building-for-other-targets)Building for other targets

[§](https://docs.rs#webassembly)WebAssembly

For WebAssembly, enable the `js` feature:

```
[dependencies.uuid]
version = "1.23.4"
features = [
    "v4",
    "v7",
    "js",
]
```
[§](https://docs.rs#embedded)Embedded

For embedded targets without the standard library, you’ll need to
disable default features when building `uuid`:

```
[dependencies.uuid]
version = "1.23.4"
default-features = false
```
Some additional features are supported in no-std environments:

- `v1`,- `v3`,- `v5`,- `v6`, and- `v8`.
- `serde`.

If you need to use `v4` or `v7` in a no-std environment, you’ll need to
produce random bytes yourself and then pass them to [ Builder::from_random_bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html#method.from_random_bytes)
without enabling the

`v4` or `v7` features.If you’re using `getrandom`, you can specify the `rng-getrandom` or `rng-rand`
features of `uuid` and configure `getrandom`’s provider per its docs. `uuid`
may upgrade its version of `getrandom` in minor releases.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Parse a UUID given in the simple format and print it as a URN:

```
let my_uuid = Uuid::parse_str("a1a2a3a4b1b2c1c2d1d2d3d4d5d6d7d8")?;
println!("{}", my_uuid.urn());
```
Generate a random UUID and print it out in hexadecimal form:

```
// Note that this requires the `v4` feature to be enabled.
let my_uuid = Uuid::new_v4();
println!("{}", my_uuid);
```
